prerequisites: Basic knowledge of high-level programming languages, e.g., in C/C++

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have a basic knowledge of the design and testing of digital circuits and their mapping to programmable logic devices using hardware description languages.

Graduates understand alternative design methodologies and can assess the underlying principles and methods. They are able to independently deepen their knowledge by incorporating current developments.
Students are able to analyze, design, and optimize combinational and sequential circuits.
Students are able to evaluate the functionality of digital components in an overall system and to develop and implement new digital systems.
After completing the module, students can select suitable methods for designing digital circuits for a given task and explain and discuss the design process.

syllabus_topics: Simulation, testing, and synthesis with an integrated development environment

assessment_methods.method: Experimental work (approx. 5 experiments of 90 min each)

bibliography: W. Gehrke, M. Winzker: Digitaltechnik. Springer-Verlag, 8. Auflage, 2023.
Peter J. Ashenden: The Designer's Guide to VHDL. Morgan Kaufmann, 2008.
